bangla_paragraph4: You see the changes in real-time and it looks just as "good" as the non-intercepted DLSS 5. Don't expect any miracles because DLSS 5 is already very compute heavy and you're adding extra overhead by running it on non-compatible hardware.Sure, both the RTX 50-series and the RX 9000 series support FP8 formats but DLSS 5 is meant to run on Tensor cores; not AMD's dual-issue AI accelerators. However, since the RTX 40-series also has Tensor cores and native FP8 support, Nvidia has confirmed that DLSS 5 will eventually make its way onto last-gen silicon as well. As for DLSS-NR-on-AMD, users have been able to get it running on RX 7000 series, but performance is once again abysmal because of the lack of FP8 support.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.The GitHub repo does mention RDNA 3 support being explored but there are no plans for it at the moment.
bangla_paragraph5: RX 9070 XT এর পারফরম্যান্স 5070 Ti এর স্তরে পৌঁছানোর জন্য অনেক কাজ করতে হবে। শেষ পর্যন্ত, মডিং সম্প্রদায়ের উচ্চাকাঙ্ক্ষা কখনই মুগ্ধ করতে ব্যর্থ হয় না কারণ এটি RDNA 4 এর উপর সবচেয়ে ধীরতম DLSS 5। এনভিডিয়ার নিজস্ব হার্ডওয়্যারে DLss 5 অনুকূল করার প্রচেষ্টা, অনিচ্ছাকৃতভাবে, এই মডটি উন্নত করবে। গুগল নিউজে টমের হার্ডওয়ার অনুসরণ করুন, অথবা আমাদের পছন্দসই উত্স হিসাবে যুক্ত করুন, আপনার ফিডে আমাদের সর্বশেষ সংবাদ, বিশ্লেষণ এবং পর্যালোচনাগুলি পেতে। হাসাম নাসি

title: Xbox Game Pass imposes monthly cloud gaming limits, just 15 hours per month for Ultimate — subscribers and non-subscribers can buy more hours to keep gaming
title_bn: এক্সবক্স গেম পাস প্রতি মাসে ক্লাউড গেমিংয়ের সীমা আরোপ করে, প্রতি মাসে মাত্র 15 ঘন্টা Ultimate এর জন্য  গ্রাহক এবং অ-অবদানকারীরা গেমিং চালিয়ে যাওয়ার জন্য আরও ঘন্টা কিনতে পারে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Microsoft has added monthly limits to its Xbox Game Pass cloud gaming service, where subscribers and non-subscribers can purchase extra playtime when they surpass their limits.
paragraph1: (Image credit: Getty Images) Xbox Game Pass has been an alternative option for gamers who cannot afford the best graphics cards. However, Microsoft has changed the business model for its cloud gaming service. The company has decided to monetize actual gaming time. Beginning in November, Game Pass subscribers will have new monthly limits on their total cloud gaming playtime. Once they reach these limits, players will be prompted to purchase additional gaming hours from the Xbox Store to keep playing.Go deeper with TH Premium: GPUsGame Pass Essential, Premium, and Ultimate subscribers will face monthly cloud playtime limits of five, 10, and 15 hours, respectively. The changes affect only Xbox Cloud Gaming, a feature included with Xbox Game Pass that lets subscribers stream and play games directly from Microsoft's servers over the Internet. Subscribers can still download and install as many Xbox Game Pass titles as they want on their consoles or gaming systems, with no monthly limits on playtime.Needless to say, Microsoft's decision marks a drastic shift for Xbox Cloud Gaming, moving from an unlimited model to a capped-hour system. Under the current packages, Game Pass Essential, Premium, and Ultimate users pay $2, $1.
paragraph2: 50, and $1.53 per hour for Xbox Cloud Gaming, respectively. Despite announcing these changes, Microsoft has yet to disclose details regarding the pricing structure for additional playtime.A hardcore gamer who subscribes to Xbox Game Pass Ultimate could easily average around 50 hours of cloud gameplay per month. For example, if they pay the highest rate ($1.53) for 35 overage hours, an Xbox Series S 512GB ($499.99) would pay for itself in under 10 months. Alternatively, the user could break even on an Xbox Series X 1TB ($749.99) in about 14 months.These changes will significantly affect heavy cloud gamers who stream games regularly.
paragraph3: Even the highest subscription tier, Game Pass Ultimate, now imposes a 15-hour monthly playtime cap. The limit is not even enough to complete one game per month. For instance, AAA titles such as Cyberpunk 2077 or Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 can take almost 30 hours to complete, even if you just stick to the main storyline.Xbox Game Pass Pricing Swipe to scroll horizontally Tier Monthly Price Xbox Cloud Gaming Monthly Hour Limit Cost Per Hour Ultimate $22.99 15 $1.53 Premium $14.99 10 $1.50 Essential $9.99 5 $2.00 The new policy introduces limits for frequent cloud gamers, but it also opens a new market for Microsoft: casual players who don't own a console or may not want to commit to a subscription but are willing to buy gaming hours to play select titles in the Xbox Game Pass library.
paragraph4: Microsoft's decision ultimately transforms Xbox Cloud Gaming into an "à la carte" type of service where gamers buy cloud playtime hours as needed.Microsoft attributes its recent policy changes to the rising infrastructure costs associated with maintaining the cloud server network. The company estimated only about 4% of its subscribers will be directly impacted by the new playtime limits. Therefore, it is reasonable to think that the other 96% of the user base do not use Xbox Cloud Gaming or stay under the monthly hour thresholds.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Over the past two years, Microsoft has implemented two price increases for Xbox Game Pass, with the most recent hike occurring in October of last year. Interestingly, despite the upward trend in pricing, the company made a surprising move by reducing the cost of Xbox Game Pass earlier this year. By shifting Xbox Cloud Gaming to a metered system, Microsoft may be trying to maintain profitability and subscriber retention.But nothing about the timing appears coincidental. Grand Theft Auto VI, arguably the most anticipated title of the decade, will launch on November 19.
paragraph5: Microsoft’s new Xbox Cloud Gaming policy is set to take effect in the very same month. Microsoft is strategically positioning the subscription service to capitalize on the massive surge of interest. The company likely wants to attract users who do not own a console or gaming system because of the ridiculous pricing but still want to play Grand Theft Auto VI. Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds. Zhiye Liu is a news editor, memory reviewer, and SSD tester at Tom’s Hardware. Although he loves everything that’s hardware, he has a soft spot for CPUs, GPUs, and RAM.

title: T-Mobile’s secret $25/month plan is tempting, but here’s why I won’t sign up
title_bn: টি-মোবাইলের গোপন ২৫ ডলার প্লেনটা বেশ প্রলুব্ধকর, কিন্তু আমি কেন সাইন আপ করবো না সেটা এখানে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: You can do a lot better than T-Mobile's new budget plan.
paragraph1: Joe Maring / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: Recently, we learned about a secret T-Mobile plan that costs just $25 per month, significantly undercutting every major US carrier. Before you rush out and sign up, however, you’ll want to make sure you understand exactly what you’re getting.On paper, the offer sounds compelling and, in a vacuum, it really is. That said, there are a few caveats you should consider before making up your mind.Is T-Mobile's new Super Essentials Saver worth signing up for?1 votesWhat is T-Mobile’s Super Essentials Saver plan?The Super Essentials Saver plan appears to offer all the features you’d get from T-Mobile’s standard Essentials plan. You get unlimited 5G data, the same 50GB of premium high-speed access, and unlimited 3G mobile hotspot usage running at 3G speeds. It even retains coverage in Mexico and Canada, alongside unlimited texting from the US to over 215 countries.So, what’s the catch? There are a few minor “gotchas.” First, the $25 price tag doesn’t include taxes and fees, which typically add another $5 to $8 per line. You are also capped at a maximum of two lines, and there is no multi-line discount.
paragraph2: Super Essentials Saver is a great deal over standard Essentials or Essentials Saver. But is it really the best option?The biggest restriction, however, is that you must be a new customer and physically visit a Walmart store to sign up, as this offer is exclusive to the big-box retailer.It’s currently unclear how long this promotion will last or whether there are any hidden downsides not immediately apparent on paper. While I haven’t found any major drawbacks compared to the standard $50 Essentials plan, be aware that you won’t see many (if any) promotional phone deals.This lack of hardware promos has largely held true for the standard Essentials tier for a while, though occasional special deals have been available in the past. It’s safe to assume this Super Saver plan will be completely devoid of promotional phone upgrades, but only time will tell.Why I’d pick Verizon Simplicity over T-Mobile’s new planJoe Maring / Android AuthorityIn many ways, Verizon Simplicity and T-Mobile Super Essentials Saver are very similar. Both plans offer an entry-level experience built around unlimited data and international roaming in Canada and Mexico.Technically, Verizon Simplicity costs $15 more per month than T-Mobile’s new Walmart plan. However, customers switching from another carrier can get it for just $30 a month. For those keeping score, that’s only $5 more than T-Mobile’s offering.While T-Mobile’s Walmart exclusive looks like a better deal at a glance, Verizon’s Simplicity plan remains the more tempting offer.
paragraph3: First, consider the line limits: while T-Mobile caps you at two lines, Verizon Simplicity allows up to 12 lines at the $30 price point. For large families, Verizon presents a much better long-term value.Verizon gives you better hotspot access and a few other extras that make it stand out — like support for up to 12 lines. Verizon doesn’t offer unlimited hotspot access, but it does include 10GB of high-speed hotspot data (even if it’s lower-priority). Verizon’s hotspot might be limited, but it will be noticeably faster than T-Mobile’s claimed 3G speeds. Most users report a cap of around 600Kbps. I’d much rather have functional, usable hotspot speeds limited to 10GB than unlimited, garbage-quality speeds any day of the week.Edgar Cervantes / Android AuthorityIf you travel frequently or live in a rural area as I do, you’ll likely find that Verizon offers the superior network, though this naturally varies depending on exactly where you live. T-Mobile’s rural coverage has improved significantly, and its main markets are among the fastest in the US, but Verizon remains more consistent nationwide.As expected with budget plans, Verizon’s base Simplicity tier doesn’t support phone promotions, meaning you’ll need to buy your phone outright or sign up for a standard payment plan. However, the Simplicity Plus and Pro add-ons offer greater upgrade flexibility for $35 and $50 per month, respectively.With these add-ons, you receive a monthly credit that covers a phone payment plan indefinitely, along with the option to upgrade annually. The cheaper Plus add-on covers phones up to $850, while the Pro tier raises that credit limit to devices valued up to $1,300.
paragraph4: While I don’t think these add-ons are worth it for most people, they highlight another area where Verizon’s plan is far more flexible than T-Mobile’s new offering.Prepaid isn’t any cheaper, but it still might be betterJoe Maring / Android AuthorityFor the first time in recent memory, two of the three largest US carriers are offering postpaid plans in the same price range as some of the cheapest unlimited prepaid plans. Because many consumers still view prepaid as a lesser experience, these budget tiers make Verizon and T-Mobile look incredibly appealing. Just be aware that paying the same price doesn’t guarantee the same experience.Postpaid plans typically hold advantages over prepaid carriers, such as more features, better financing options, and superior device insurance. The catch here is that T-Mobile and Verizon have dramatically watered down the features and phone promotions on these budget plans. You are mostly paying for the brand name, as the standard postpaid perks simply don’t apply or are heavily restricted.Visible and other prepaid carriers might not cost any less, but many of these plans offer extras that the cheaper Verizon and T-Mobile plans are lacking. While Verizon and T-Mobile’s high-end plans absolutely outcompete a prepaid option like Visible Plus in terms of features, the opposite is true at this budget tier. With Visible Plus, you currently pay $29 per month, including taxes and fees.For that price, you get true HD video streaming, rather than the 720p cap typical of budget postpaid offerings. You also get unlimited premium data and unlimited hotspot access capped at a very usable 10Mbps. Furthermore, the international data options are vastly superior.
paragraph5: Not only do you get unlimited talk, text, and data in Mexico and Canada, but you also receive one Global Pass day per month (which can accrue up to 12 days).Visible is arguably one of the best overall values right now in both the prepaid and postpaid markets, but you’ll find a similarly competitive experience with prepaid carriers like US Mobile or Mint Mobile.Which is the right pick for you?Edgar Cervantes / Android AuthorityPersonally, I’d gladly take Verizon or Visible over T-Mobile’s new plan. The “Un-carrier” has always been less impressive in my rural Midwestern neck of the woods, and the potential $5 in monthly savings isn’t worth giving up Verizon’s network reliability.If your situation sounds similar, I highly recommend looking closer at prepaid options. The same advice applies if you want to spend under $40 per month but still want premium features like better international coverage, high-priority data, and usable hotspot speeds. The major carriers offer all of these perks, but you’ll pay close to triple the price to get them on a standard postpaid plan.That said, some users are absolutely set on sticking to a major brand for perceived advantages, such as marginally better customer support, simple installment plans, or specific add-ons and insurance. In those cases, Verizon Simplicity is the clear winner.Ultimately, unless you absolutely prefer T-Mobile’s network in your specific region, you are likely better off looking elsewhere.FollowThank you for being part of our community. title: We tested DLSS 5 in NBA 2K27 with every RTX 50-series GPU — first official release comes with a big performance hit, but almost every Blackwell card can run it at 1080p
title_bn: আমরা এনবিএ ২কে২৭-এ DLSS ৫-কে প্রতিটি RTX ৫০-সিরিজের জিপিইউ-র সাথে পরীক্ষা করেছি  প্রথম আনুষ্ঠানিক রিলিজটি বড় পারফরম্যান্স হিটের সাথে আসে কিন্তু প্রায় প্রতিটি ব্ল্যাকওয়েল কার্ড এটি 1080p-এ চালাতে পারে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: We tested Nvidia's DLSS 5 in NBA 2K27 across every RTX 50-series graphics card at 1080p, 1440p, and 4K to see just how much performance it costs to explore the frontiers of neural rendering.
paragraph1: (Image credit: 2K) Nvidia's DLSS 5 has arrived in NBA 2K27, and we've been up since midnight testing it across every RTX 50-series graphics card to see what the first official implementation of this tech can do and how it compares to the community-implemented mods that have been circulating over the past couple weeks.Before we discuss the performance cost of DLSS 5, many will ask whether this tech is even worth getting excited about, given the intense controversy that it's sparked ever since Nvidia revealed it earlier this year.In short: yes, absolutely.This first-party implementation of DLSS 5, tuned under the full control of 2K Games' art directors and artists, looks incredible, full stop. If you see it running, you will want to leave it on. It doesn't look like "slop" or a cheap filter. It just looks correct, or at least more correct. Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: 2K) For just a couple of examples, without DLSS 5, even at ultra settings and with RT, the game has a slightly "plastic" or "flat" look. Faces can have a waxy uniformity that immediately indicates that you're looking at a video game, not a live broadcast. Hair looks totally and unnaturally flat. The whites of eyes can be unnaturally bright, giving a sort of googly-eye or doll-like effect that immediately broke my sense of immersion. I didn't think any of this would be a big deal for a sports game, but it all stands out.
paragraph2: Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: 2K) DLSS 5 breathes incredible life into NBA 2K27. Skin looks like real flesh and blood. Eyes are rendered with the proper tones, depth, and sparkle. Hair looks a billion times more realistic. Every human on screen just looks more alive. You won't entirely forget that you're looking at a game, but it becomes much easier to suspend disbelief and get lost in the action.My experience slapping DLSS 5 mods into games has produced promising but sometimes mixed results. If the polished experience that NBA 2K25 delivers is any indication, I can't wait for more studios to get their hands on it and integrate it into their games under the care of the same artists that created them.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Our testing methodsWe did our best to deliver clean test numbers in the short time we've had with NBA 2K27. Performance in this can be tricky to measure. Benchmarking in the hub worlds or cutscenes will deliver lower performance than on the court, and even then, in-game events like fouls and time-outs will also result in skewed numbers if you're not careful.
paragraph3: We picked a repeatable match-up from the game's career mode and sampled 60 seconds of continuous gameplay with DLSS 5 on and off, making sure to restart if we ran into any of the scripted events above.We used NBA 2K27's maximum graphics settings as our baseline, including RT. We tested at native resolutions without upscaling, and we didn't test with Multi Frame Generation enabled. We view MFG as a cherry on top of an already solid baseline experience, not a baseline in itself.Our test system is built with the following components: Swipe to scroll horizontally Tom's Hardware 2026 GPU Test System CPU AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D CPU Cooler Thermalright Phantom Spirit 120SE Memory 32GB (2x16GB) G.Skill Trident Z5 Neo DDR5-6000 CL30 Motherboard Asus TUF Gaming X670E-Plus Wifi Storage Inland Performance Plus 4TB PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD Power supply MSI MPG Ai1600TS 1600W Operating system Windows 11 Pro Graphics driver version GeForce Game Ready 616.64 All of our performance results are captured using Nvidia's FrameView 2.0 utility. We measure graphics card power consumption directly with Nvidia's PCAT hardware power logging tool.If you have any questions about our testing methods, let us know in the comments and we'll do our best to answer them. On to the numbers.
paragraph4: NBA 2K27 1080p performance (Image credit: Future)At 1080p, everything from the RTX 5070 on up is CPU-bound without DLSS 5 enabled, even with maxed-out settings and RT on. Turn on DLSS 5, though, and the differences in Tensor Core compute across the cards quickly becomes obvious. But even the RTX 5060 can manage nearly 60 FPS on average with DLSS 5 enabled at 1080p, so almost anybody with a Blackwell card can at least try out the feature.Given these results, you might think to enable DLSS Super Resolution (aka upscaling). But because the amount of time needed to run the DLSS 5 model has a fixed cost per output frame that scales with your target resolution and largely dominates the total frame time, especially on lower-end hardware, you may find that enabling DLSS SR doesn't have as much of an effect on performance as we've come to expect. The game still has to wait for that final generative step to occur, even if DLSS SR cuts down some of the total frame time.As noted, we didn't use MFG for these tests, simply because there's no need for us to make the numbers on these charts artifically large. If you do want to enable it, the multiplier you want will be determined by your monitor's refresh rate and your own personal tastes. (Image credit: Future)We did chart PC latency as estimated by FrameView, so you can get a sense of whether there's enough of a latency budget to enable MFG at all. At 1080p, every card is a solid candidate for enabling MFG without adding unreasonable amounts of input latency, although the RTX 5050 is in a borderline position. And all three of the 8GB cards might have trouble fitting the MFG model into their VRAM with these maxed-out settings and DLSS 5 enabled, so you might need to turn off RT at a minimum to use MFG on these lower-end GPUs. (Image credit: Future)As we already saw in early testing of the leaked DLSS 5 builds circulating in the community, enabling the model has a large impact on power consumption, likely due to the intense Tensor Core load required to run the DLSS 5 model.
paragraph5: NBA 2K27 1440p performance (Image credit: Future)Moving up to 1440p separates our cards some more. The RTX 5080 and RTX 5090 are still CPU-limited without DLSS 5. The RTX 5060 Ti 8GB, RTX 5060, and RTX 5050 all get a "Low VRAM" warning with these settings, so if you're trying to push this higher resolution with those cards, you might want to start tuning your DLSS upscaling settings to relieve VRAM pressure, even if it doesn't result in additional performance with DLSS 5. (Image credit: Future)But you really want an RTX 5060 Ti at a minimum here to get acceptable input latency with DLSS 5 enabled, and the RTX 5070 is the true baseline for a good experience. At the higher end, the RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 5080 both provide fluid frame rates even without MFG, and you have the latency budget to enable framegen without worry on anything from the RTX 5070 on up. (Image credit: Future)DLSS 5's power consumption on all these cards (except the chugging RTX 5050) rises as expected with the higher-resolution output frame we're asking it to generate. Everything from the RTX 5060 up to the RTX 5070 Ti ends up running at its power limit, while the RTX 5080 and RTX 5090 still have room to stretch out. The unconstrained MSI RTX 5090 Lighting Z sucks down a ton of power to deliver its scorching performance.NBA 2K27 4K performance (Image credit: Future)Running NBA 2K27 at 4K with DLSS 5 is extremely demanding, since the model has to generate an output frame with more than twice as many pixels than at 1440p. Even the RTX 5070 Ti is straining here, as its input latency with DLSS 5 is potentially too high to enable MFG while still delivering a responsive gameplay experience. (Image credit: Future)You can see why Nvidia only recommends the RTX 5080 and RTX 5090 for a 4K DLSS 5 experience in this title, as they're the only two cards that deliver high enough baseline performance with low enough input latencies to make MFG practical.

But because the amount of time needed to run the DLSS 5 model has a fixed cost per output frame that scales with your target resolution and largely dominates the total frame time, especially on lower-end hardware, you may find that enabling DLSS SR doesn't have as much of an effect on performance as we've come to expect. The game still has to wait for that final generative step to occur, even if DLSS SR cuts down some of the total frame time.As noted, we didn't use MFG for these tests, simply because there's no need for us to make the numbers on these charts artifically large. If you do want to enable it, the multiplier you want will be determined by your monitor's refresh rate and your own personal tastes. (Image credit: Future)We did chart PC latency as estimated by FrameView, so you can get a sense of whether there's enough of a latency budget to enable MFG at all. At 1080p, every card is a solid candidate for enabling MFG without adding unreasonable amounts of input latency, although the RTX 5050 is in a borderline position. And all three of the 8GB cards might have trouble fitting the MFG model into their VRAM with these maxed-out settings and DLSS 5 enabled, so you might need to turn off RT at a minimum to use MFG on these lower-end GPUs. (Image credit: Future)As we already saw in early testing of the leaked DLSS 5 builds circulating in the community, enabling the model has a large impact on power consumption, likely due to the intense Tensor Core load required to run the DLSS 5 model.
bangla_paragraph5: NBA 2K27 1440p performance (Image credit: Future)Moving up to 1440p separates our cards some more. The RTX 5080 and RTX 5090 are still CPU-limited without DLSS 5. The RTX 5060 Ti 8GB, RTX 5060, and RTX 5050 all get a "Low VRAM" warning with these settings, so if you're trying to push this higher resolution with those cards, you might want to start tuning your DLSS upscaling settings to relieve VRAM pressure, even if it doesn't result in additional performance with DLSS 5. (Image credit: Future)But you really want an RTX 5060 Ti at a minimum here to get acceptable input latency with DLSS 5 enabled, and the RTX 5070 is the true baseline for a good experience. At the higher end, the RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 5080 both provide fluid frame rates even without MFG, and you have the latency budget to enable framegen without worry on anything from the RTX 5070 on up. (Image credit: Future)DLSS 5's power consumption on all these cards (except the chugging RTX 5050) rises as expected with the higher-resolution output frame we're asking it to generate. Everything from the RTX 5060 up to the RTX 5070 Ti ends up running at its power limit, while the RTX 5080 and RTX 5090 still have room to stretch out. The unconstrained MSI RTX 5090 Lighting Z sucks down a ton of power to deliver its scorching performance.NBA 2K27 4K performance (Image credit: Future)Running NBA 2K27 at 4K with DLSS 5 is extremely demanding, since the model has to generate an output frame with more than twice as many pixels than at 1440p. Even the RTX 5070 Ti is straining here, as its input latency with DLSS 5 is potentially too high to enable MFG while still delivering a responsive gameplay experience. (Image credit: Future)You can see why Nvidia only recommends the RTX 5080 and RTX 5090 for a 4K DLSS 5 experience in this title, as they're the only two cards that deliver high enough baseline performance with low enough input latencies to make MFG practical.

title: Robotaxis enter their villain era
title_bn: রোবোট্যাক্সি তাদের দুষ্টু যুগে প্রবেশ করে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: It's Bullitt meets Christine meets Waymo. A new short film imagines a San Francisco car chase where the other driver isn't human - and the car may be trying to kill you. That a robotaxi can now be cast as the villain with almost no explanation says s
paragraph1: It’s Bullitt meets Christine meets Waymo.A new short film imagines a San Francisco car chase where the other driver isn’t human — and the car may be trying to kill you. That a robotaxi can now be cast as the villain with almost no explanation says something about the present moment. Autonomous cars have gone from sci-fi curiosities to fixtures in some American cities, where they’ve become stand-ins for anxieties about AI job displacement, Big Tech surveillance, and machines making decisions once left to humans.Road Rage, the planned short film awaiting $40,000 on Kickstarter to fund production, leans into all of it. The film pits Joa, a ridehail driver in a manual-transmission car, against Roboride, an autonomous vehicle that takes a minor road-rage incident very personally, according to a synopsis by its director, Romain Thomassin. Roboride lightly clips Joa’s mirror. Joa gives it the finger. The car decides to kill him.“It’s analog versus artificial,” Thomassin told The Verge.The AI bad guy will be played by an old Prius transformed with cold LED lights across the front — à la Tesla — fake cameras, a spinning lidar-like device on the roof, a black exterior, and a menacing, ever-blinking red dot. Thomassin calls the intended result a “nasty Waymo.”“I really wanted to play the nasty, gritty look of the ’70s car chase, but with today’s robotaxi in today’s San Francisco,” he said.
paragraph2: The chase itself will be a throwback: real cars, real actors, and real stunts.“I really wanted to play the nasty, gritty look of the ’70s car chase, but with today’s robotaxi in today’s San Francisco.”— Road Rage director Romain Thomassin“What makes Joa the good guy is not only his instinct but also his authenticity,” Thomassin said, noting a scene in which the character has an unexpected conversation with his passengers. “This type of human interaction doesn’t happen in a robotaxi.”Thomassin doesn’t actually think robotaxis are inherently evil. But as a movie villain, they come preloaded with tension. For one thing, they’re replacing the kind of worker his protagonist represents. Joa is a Mexican immigrant trying to make a living driving in an increasingly expensive San Francisco. Robotaxis are already competing with ridehail drivers, just as generative AI is competing with workers in Thomassin’s own industry.“Driving here is a metaphor for what’s happening in cinema, in filmmaking,” Thomassin said.1/4Guerilla posters for Road Rage. Image: Grace Vincent / Road RageThen there’s surveillance. Autonomous cars are covered in cameras and sensors, constantly observing the streets — and people — around them.
paragraph3: That, more than the prospect of being driven around without a human behind the wheel, is what actually unnerves Thomassin.In Road Rage, that anxiety is pushed toward dystopia. There’s a brief encounter involving immigration enforcement, and Thomassin imagines a feature-length version in which autonomous cars identify people, trap passengers inside, or deliver them directly to authorities. The progression, as he describes it, is observation, surveillance, then control.“The next step is that [autonomous vehicles] could become the police,” he said. And because robotaxis operate as connected fleets, the threat can scale beyond one vehicle. “Imagine an army rising up,” Thomassin said.Robotaxis also make unusually good revenge-movie villains because people already treat them like adversaries. Thomassin points to the indignities Waymos have endured on San Francisco streets: people immobilizing them with traffic cones, tagging and vandalizing them, and even setting them on fire.“They are being bullied,” he said. In Road Rage, that mistreatment becomes the motivation: “They want to take revenge.”Thomassin describes Roboride as absorbing the behavior it observes around it — including the behavior of human drivers. The car is simply learning road rage from humans.
paragraph4: “Humans are known to be the worst versions of themselves on the road,” he said.That makes Roboride a very 2026 update to the killer car idea in Stephen King’s Christine. There, the menace is supernatural. Here, it comes from something more contemporary: a machine that watches humans, learns from them, and inherits some of their worst traits along with the useful ones.On the other side of the chase is Joa and his stick shift — a deliberately analog counterpoint. To Thomassin, driving stick is a deeply human act: The driver remains in control of the vehicle, physically responding to the road. What separates Joa from Roboride, in Thomassin’s telling, is instinct — and even irrationality.During one confrontation, Joa takes his hands off the steering wheel while facing down the autonomous car. The move is so reckless that Roboride backs off. The human wins by becoming less predictable than the machine.“Respect your madness. Be a little mad and creative in your way of doing things, and you will be able to rise against the machines.”— Romain Thomassin“Respect your madness,” Thomassin said.
paragraph5: “Be a little mad and creative in your way of doing things, and you will be able to rise against the machines.”Despite its skepticism toward AI, Road Rage may use some of the technology itself. Thomassin says the filmmakers are considering AI-generated imagery to depict what Roboride sees, while shooting the human driver’s world with traditional cinematography. To him, that distinction matters. He sees AI as a creative tool when it serves the story, rather than simply a way to replace workers.For all the menace he sees in robotaxis, Thomassin isn’t afraid to ride in them. He signed up for Waymo as soon as he could and uses it when visiting friends and family for rides.“I don’t feel in danger,” he said.That may be what makes Roboride such an effective 2026 villain. The scary part isn’t necessarily that the machine will crash. The scary part is that the machine works.Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.
